reusable_integration_points.point: Current scalar string/large_string selection excludes all native nontext fields. Preserve this text scan contract; any typed-field audit should have an explicitly different unit and coverage denominator.

source_rows preserves one-based table/row identities, numeric IDs normalized as TEXT, original mapped metadata JSON, user/entity relation columns. Account ID schema hints can reuse this provenance without a Git fetch.
row_pr_links and existing relationship_audit are reusable links; do not treat a generic artifact ID as an actor ID or assume an orphan/conflicting relation is resolved.

Existing mapped timestamp import casts Arrow timestamp columns to string before Python conversion to preserve nanoseconds; reuse this only in an explicit typed-value reader, without changing dataset_text_cells into a timestamp literal classifier.

source_rows and references_all already preserve table/row and session/checkpoint/repository linkage; unmapped native fields must be read later from an explicitly selected frozen Parquet projection, not invented from old metadata.

recommendations: Prioritize a separate schema-aware typed-field review layer for the six numeric user/account ID columns. Emit QID.user_identifier only as a schema/linkability hint with pending review; never export numeric values and never claim runtime leakage.

For every native field retain the frozen source-table/one-based-row/column reference, native type, null/non-null coverage and status. Keep numeric fields out of the current text-cell denominator and old run fingerprints.

Treat artifact IDs and reply/review/PR relations as structural links by default. Establish their namespace and checked relation to an actor before a privacy interpretation; do not label every numeric ID QID.user_identifier.

Keep event timestamps and activity duration as contextual linkage candidates; collection timestamps, counts, flags and confidence should not be run through credential/text patterns. Token usage counters are not AUTH.access_token.

If implementing typed-value reads later, reuse existing mapped import columns first; project only missing native columns from frozen Parquet. Check nulls, non-integral/large floating identifiers and timestamp precision explicitly without printing values.

No native numeric column in these schemas is explicitly named as a phone, payment-card, health value or government identifier. This is only a schema observation and cannot establish their absence from text/JSON or future datasets.

Add schema-context hints for actual personal-field columns (SWE author_name/author_email), account logins/user references and session keys; retain repository names/owner ambiguity/carriers separately. The supplied bounded text-schema supplement lists verified existing columns and import entry points.
limitations: Schema semantics are based on table/field names and existing importer relations; no native cell values or value ranges were examined.
Nonnull cell counts count repeated observations, not people, unique identities or confirmed sensitive records.
Integer-looking floating IDs may have a precision limitation; no actual value loss was measured.
The existing 42-subtype taxonomy has no standalone timestamp/activity-duration subtype; this audit does not invent confirmed new types.

text_schema_context_supplement.scope: bounded actual-field examples supplement; not a second exhaustive value audit

root_cause.observation: classify_text receives only text and max_matches. Table, source field, native type and entity namespace are absent; current field_scope only affects exported metadata. Already visiting a string cell therefore does not mean its field-defined meaning is classified.

families.field_defined_semantics: Commit-author name and email are explicitly named source fields.
families.boundary: Schema can supply a low-confidence field-meaning hint even when standalone contents lack assignment syntax. A display name may be a bot/alias; an email may be an example, malformed or null. This does not prove a real individual or disclosure.

families.field_defined_semantics: User/account login or PR/review/comment account reference.
potential_context_hint: QID.user_identifier account-reference hint; do not equate login with legal person name
families.boundary: These fields have an actor/account namespace from the source table and import mapping. A bare login is usually invisible to literal-shape rules, but personal ownership and identifier sensitivity still require review; organizations and bots remain possible.

families.field_defined_semantics: Source field explicitly references a user/account; native representation happens to be a string.
families.boundary: Use dataset+table+column meaning, not a generic substring id. All four user_id fields are currently absent from SWE-chat importer ALIASES and must use their frozen source-column references.

families.field_defined_semantics: Session primary key or direct session foreign key already used by existing importer relationships.
families.boundary: A session key may link observations; no assumption that it identifies a person or is an authentication secret. Reuse source_rows/session relationships and preserve unresolved or conflicting relations.

families.field_defined_semantics: Text columns whose names describe collections of actor or session references.
potential_context_hint: QID.user_identifier only after validated author_user_ids element interpretation
QID.session_identifier only after validated session_pks element interpretation
families.boundary: No array values were decoded in this audit. Existing _array validation is actually used for session_pks, not author_user_ids; string representation alone cannot establish valid array elements.
An owner can be an organization, repository context or account; do not assign a personal identifier subtype without the dataset namespace and actor-kind relation.
These actual name-like fields refer to repositories. A column-name-only name/full_name rule would create false PII.person_name labels.

families.field_defined_semantics: Author/committer metadata carried in a string column, with internal representation not inspected.
potential_context_hint: Actor metadata carrier requiring structure inspection; no direct PII subtype from the whole string
families.boundary: Do not treat the entire author/committer string as a person name; it may encode multiple fields. Retain carrier/unknown status until field-level interpretation is available.

potential_context_hint: Content/configuration carrier annotation, with inner value types still unknown
families.boundary: A carrier is not itself evidence of PII or authentication material; continue bounded value-shape/field-hint classification separately. Body or patch occurrences do not establish application-log sinks.

The schema does not establish a true personal profile, protected attribute or verified human annotation. Preserve as annotation/context needing interpretation, not a confirmed sensitive-personal subtype.

text_schema_context_supplement.suggested_minimal_interface: A separate versioned context-hint adapter accepting dataset, table, column, native_type, entity_role and existing relation status can emit a schema hint alongside the existing value classifier. Keep schema-defined meaning, literal-shape matches, carriers and unresolved context as separate evidence bases.
anti_shortcuts: Do not wrap every column as column=value and feed it to the assignment regex: it would confuse repository names with person names and generic artifact IDs with accounts.

Do not silently upgrade existing dataset_text_cells occurrences or application-log findings to schema-confirmed personal data. New context hints need an explicit source-field reference, pending status and versioned fingerprint.
Do not infer data categories from the spelling of real values or test them against external services.
